anomalies.observed: R6 (10K) is connected between VCC and the MCU-side TACH net, which also goes to U2.3/U3.3 and the left side of R4. D1 (5V1) is connected from the fan-side node (J2.3 and the right side of R4) to GND. The pull-up and clamp are on opposite sides of R4, with the pull-up on the MCU side and the clamp on the fan side.
anomalies.expected: For a 12V open-collector fan tach signal into a 5V MCU, the pull-up should be on the fan-side node (to VCC) and the zener should clamp the MCU-side TACH net to GND, or the pull-up should be to +5V on the MCU side. The zener must protect the MCU input, not the fan side.

evidence.quote: R6 10K connected to VCC and TACH; D1 5V1 from J2.3/R4.2 to GND; U2 ATtiny45-20P pin3 TACH

anomalies.impact: When the fan's open-collector TACH output is high/open, the ATtiny TACH pin can be pulled toward VCC (likely 12V), exceeding its absolute maximum. The 5.1V zener does not clamp the MCU side because it is separated by R4, so the pin may be damaged or tach readings may be unreliable.

parsed.summary: The schematic contains a TACH interface error: the 10K pull-up R6 is on the MCU side of the series resistor while the 5.1V zener D1 clamps the fan side, so the ATtiny TACH input is not protected from the higher VCC rail. This is the main anomaly.
